units.passage: AI and AI add-ins cannot be used in video conference sessions unless all participants are aware of the use and agree to not disclose any Personal Information or Protected Information.
units.why: 'AI and AI add-ins cannot be used in video conference sessions unless all participants are aware of the use and agree'; consent for AI in meetings, P86.
units.fit_note: Participants must also agree not to disclose personal or protected information.

units.passage: Be cognizant of virtual meetings where AI meeting tools may be used, inquire with the meeting host about the use of these tools if unsure, and decline participation in the meeting if the host insists on using these tools.
units.why: Researchers should "inquire with the meeting host" and "decline participation" if the host insists on AI tools. Consent-style rule, P86.

units.passage: They should also avoid using GenAI-automated meeting tools to record or capture discussions involving sensitive data or topics.
units.why: Researchers should 'avoid using GenAI-automated meeting tools to record or capture discussions involving sensitive data'. Rule on AI recording of meetings, P86.
units.fit_note: Limited to discussions with sensitive data; no consent mechanism is described.

units.passage: If a host insists on using GenAI-automated tools despite concerns, UMD researchers are advised to decline participation to protect institutional data integrity and privacy.
units.why: If a host insists on AI meeting tools, researchers "are advised to decline participation", a companion rule on AI recording, P86.
units.fit_note: Advises declining participation rather than seeking consent.

units.passage: Consent – when GenAI is used as a virtual presence, such as serving as a virtual meeting attendee or transcription service to capture and summarize meeting discussion, wiretapping laws may be violated in jurisdictions (such as Massachusetts) that require prior consent of the parties
units.why: Using GenAI as a virtual attendee or transcriber "may" violate Massachusetts wiretapping law requiring "prior consent", a consent rule for AI recording (P86).
units.fit_note: Frames consent as a legal risk (wiretapping laws) rather than a direct rule.

units.passage: • Using AI to transcribe or summarize course lectures. • Uploading instructor-created course materials to an AI tool for the purposes of summary generation.
units.policy: Unless specifically approved by Student Accessibility Services, students may not use AI to transcribe or summarize course lectures.
units.why: Sample text prohibits 'Using AI to transcribe or summarize course lectures' unless SAS approves; P86 covers AI transcription of class sessions, though here it is a ban with an SAS exception rather than a consent rule.
units.fit_note: Covers summarizing as well as transcribing; the exception is approval by Student Accessibility Services rather than consent, and the ban does not concern recording consent.

units.passage: The campus does not offer an enterprise solution at this time and prohibits the use of free AI tools to record, transcribe and/or summarize meetings.
units.why: The campus 'prohibits the use of free AI tools to record, transcribe and/or summarize meetings', which is a ban on unapproved AI recording (P86).
units.fit_note: Ban on free tools; no enterprise tool is offered. Consent is mentioned only as a complication.

units.passage: If you are using an AI notetaker, it is important that you inform the other participants of the meeting of that use.
units.why: "it is important that you inform the other participants of the meeting of that use" requires announcing AI notetaker use, which is consent before AI recording (P86).

units.passage: Students should make sure use of an AI notetaker in class is permitted by the instructor.
units.why: "Students should make sure use of an AI notetaker in class is permitted by the instructor" requires student permission before AI recording in class, P86 with student actor.

units.passage: Internal and closed meetings may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized, secured and managed by IRT
units.why: The sentence 'Internal and closed meetings may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized, secured and managed by IRT' limits which platform may record meetings. It is not coursework or study, so phase is general. Everyone who records meetings is bound, modality is must, and P86 (recording and transcription) is the nearest type.
units.fit_note: Condition is IRT authorization, not consent of participants. | Requires IRT authorization of the recording platform rather than consent of participants.

units.passage: AI transcriptions of confidential Human Resources meetings, including candidate interviews, should not be used except in circumstances where prior Human Resources permission has been obtained and appropriate safeguards are implemented on transcriptions created
units.why: The passage 'AI transcriptions of confidential Human Resources meetings, including candidate interviews, should not be used' applies to anyone who would transcribe an HR meeting, and it is not coursework, so actor is all and phase is general. 'Should not be used' gives should-not and P86 is the nearest type (AI recording and transcription).

units.passage: Ensure that, at the beginning of the meeting, all meeting participants are aware of and consent to the meeting being recorded / transcribed. Only begin recording once all participants have consented.
units.policy: Ensure that, at the beginning of the meeting, all meeting participants are aware of and consent to the meeting being recorded / transcribed, and begin recording only once all participants have consented.
units.why: Recorded or transcribed meetings require that 'all meeting participants are aware of and consent'; consent before AI recording, P86.

units.passage: Students must obtain prior approval from the instructor before recording any lectures, whether in audio or video format. Unauthorized recording is strictly prohibited and may result in disciplinary action in accordance with university policies
units.why: "Students must obtain prior approval from the instructor before recording any lectures" is a consent rule for recording; nearest P86 though it is not AI-specific in wording.
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI recording or transcription; appears within the AI policy framework. Applies to any recording of lectures, not only AI recording or transcription.

units.passage: in the same way that we notify others that we are recording a Teams or Zoom meeting, we should be transparent if we have an AI taking notes.
units.policy: We should be transparent if we have an AI taking notes, in the same way that we notify others that we are recording a Teams or Zoom meeting.
units.why: "we should be transparent if we have an AI taking notes" parallels telling people about recording; consent or notice before AI transcription, so P86.
units.fit_note: It asks for notice, not explicit permission, before AI note-taking.

units.passage: Students may not use AI-powered tools for note-taking, transcription, recording, meeting-assistant, or summarization tools
units.why: Students 'may not use AI-powered tools for note-taking, transcription, recording' without 'the instructor's prior written permission' - a consent rule for AI recording, P86.

units.passage: may not be shared, posted, distributed, uploaded to another AI system, or retained beyond the end of the course
units.why: Authorized AI summaries 'may not be shared, posted, distributed, uploaded to another AI system, or retained beyond the end of the course', limiting what students can do with recordings; closest is P86 (recording rules) though it is about downstream use.
units.fit_note: Concerns recordings and AI summaries of class, plus sharing and retention limits. / Covers sharing, uploading to another AI, and retention of authorized recordings, not recording consent itself. / Concerns what may be done with authorized recordings, transcripts and AI summaries (no sharing, no upload to another AI system, no retention beyond the course), not consent to record.

units.passage: If a student, faculty member, employee, or researcher intends to use such a tool and it records spoken conversations, they must provide notice, such as including it in a syllabus or announcing its use before recording.
units.why: Anyone using an AI notetaking tool that records speech "must provide notice, such as including it in a syllabus or announcing its use"; consent/notice before AI recording, P86.

units.passage: If an individual objects to being recorded, an alternative note-taking method should be explored and considered.
units.why: "If an individual objects to being recorded, an alternative note-taking method should be explored"; an objection accommodation, P86.
